gaps.sentence: He is under a lot of ___ at work (PRESS).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'a lot of'; fixed phrase 'under ___'
gaps.explanation: 'Under pressure' is the fixed phrase; the noun of 'press' is 'pressure'.

gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.

gaps.sentence: This grant will ___ her to study abroad (ABLE).
gaps.hint: positive verb needed: make it possible (en-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix en- forms the verb: enable means to make able. 'Disable' is the negative opposite.
After 'complete' a noun is needed: darkness (-ness noun of 'dark').

gaps.sentence: She is very ___ in modern art (INTEREST).
gaps.hint: how she feels: -ed; fixed pattern '___ in'
gaps.explanation: 'Interested in something' describes the person's feeling; 'interesting' describes the thing that causes it.
A bank manager is a person; 'management' is the activity and 'manage' is the verb.

gaps.sentence: Don't ___ your children — let them make their own mistakes (PROTECT).
gaps.hint: protect too much (over-); a base verb is needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means excessively: overprotect means to protect too much. A base verb follows 'Don't'.

gaps.sentence: The airline is known for its excellent ___ (SERVE).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'excellent'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'serve' is 'service' (-ice); a servant is a person who serves.
